newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steady in deathly quiet market.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steady in deathly quiet market.

text.p: NWE gasoline was steady on Wednesday in an extremely dull market, traders said.
"It's deathly," said one trader. "There's nothing going on."
Traders assessed Eurograde barges around $206/$208 fob ARA for prompt material while first half June was around $207/$209 for running refinery and $207/$208.50 for fob Rotterdam.
"People really aren't sure where the market's going so they're taking a wait and see approach," said one trader.
American Petroleum Institute (API) data and EIA data out on Tuesday and Wednesday respectively had given little direction, traders said.
According to API data U.S. gasoline stocks rose by 837,000 barrels last week while reformulated gasoline stocks fell 1.38 million barrels.
While Department of Energy data showed gasoline stocks were up 400,000 barrels and reformulated gasoline stocks were down 1.4 million barrels.
"The API's haven't had too much of an impact," said one trader. "I see them as mildly bearish."
Traders said plenty of material was finding its way across the Atlantic with estimates that 150-200,000 tonnes would move to the United States between May 15 to June 5.
There was little talk on the cargo front, although prices remained relatively high.

A cargo offered at $217.50 cif NWE on Tuesday was unsighted on Wednesday, but traders said they did not think it had been sold. They assessed price levels for such a cargo was around $217/$218.50 cif NWE.
